question: How is the autonomic nervous system different from the somatic nervous system?

options.A: The autonomic system is completely independent and never interacts with the brain.
options.B: The autonomic system controls involuntary organs while the somatic controls voluntary muscles.
options.C: The autonomic system only uses sensory neurons while the somatic uses motor neurons.
options.D: The autonomic system is located in the brain while the somatic is in the spinal cord.

explanation: Spot on! Somatic nerves let you move your arms and legs on purpose, while autonomic pathways handle the behind-the-scenes organs that work without your direct control. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: A nurse working in a rural primary health clinic notices an increase in skin infections among children. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Close the clinic permanently until a modern hospital is built nearby
options.B: Investigate local hygiene practices and provide health education on hand washing
options.C: Order expensive laboratory tests from overseas for every sick child
options.D: Tell parents that skin infections cannot be prevented in rural areas

explanation: The nurse begins by assessing the community's hygiene habits and teaching simple, effective prevention strategies to stop the outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h8)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely on just one method to check a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Patients usually refuse to answer dietary recall questionnaires alone
options.B: Hospital policies strictly require at least four different diagnostic tests
options.C: Lab values and physical signs can be influenced by acute illness or hydration
options.D: Single methods are too expensive for routine primary health clinics

explanation: Things like fluid changes can mess with lab numbers quickly, so combining a few tools gives you a much clearer, more reliable picture. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why are sharps containers made with hard, thick plastic walls?

options.A: To allow the containers to be reused multiple times safely
options.B: To dissolve the metal needles chemically inside the box
options.C: To make the bins heavy enough to stay upright on carts
options.D: To prevent needles from piercing through and injuring handlers

explanation: Spot on! Those tough walls ensure used needles won't accidentally poke right through and stick anyone handling the box. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To lower the financial cost of operating public hospitals
options.B: To reduce the number of working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To develop knowledge for nursing practice and improve patient outcomes
options.D: To replace physicians in diagnosing complex medical conditions

explanation: Nursing research focuses on building a scientific base for nursing care so patients receive the safest and most effective interventions. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: A nurse manager wants to check the exact number of patient falls on the ward last year. What type of study is this?

options.A: Descriptive research
options.B: Exploratory research
options.C: Experimental laboratory research
options.D: Basic research

explanation: Exactly! Descriptive research simply counts and describes characteristics or events, like keeping track of how many patient falls occurred. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why do so many teenagers today end up low on vitamin D?

options.A: Consuming too many citrus fruits and juices
options.B: Drinking excessive amounts of plain water
options.C: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.D: Spending less time outdoors in natural sunlight

explanation: You nailed it! Our bodies make vitamin D from sunlight on the skin. With more indoor time and screen sessions, teens get less natural sun exposure. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h4)

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar comes back at 115 mg/dL. How should you interpret this?

options.A: It confirms active type 1 diabetes
options.B: It is a completely normal result
options.C: It indicates prediabetes and impaired fasting glucose
options.D: It shows the patient had severe low blood sugar

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL sit in the prediabetic zone. It's a great warning sign for patients to adjust their diet and lifestyle early! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h5)

question: What is the core question asked during a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigation?

options.A: Which specific staff member is guilty of negligence?
options.B: Why did the system allow this event to happen?
options.C: How much financial loss did the hospital suffer?
options.D: Who should be fired immediately for this failure?

explanation: RCA is like detective work for processes—we look for broken systems, not bad people. [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the main idea behind family-centred care when nursing an infant?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to make all home care choices
options.B: Treating the infant as part of a family unit
options.C: Focusing solely on the medical needs of the baby
options.D: Isolating the infant from other family members

explanation: Spot on! Family-centred care treats the baby and the family as one team, making sure you work closely with the loved ones who know the child best. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is the main job of red blood cells (erythrocytes) in our body?

options.A: Releasing antibodies during an allergic reaction
options.B: Transporting oxygen to body tissues
options.C: Forming initial plugs to stop bleeding
options.D: Fighting off bacterial infections

explanation: Awesome! Red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, acting like tiny delivery vans that pick up oxygen in the lungs and drop it off all over the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why might someone with diabetes and failing kidneys suddenly need less insulin than before?

options.A: Damaged kidneys fail to clear circulating insulin from the blood
options.B: Muscle tissue begins burning glucose much faster than normal
options.C: The liver stops storing glucose as glycogen
options.D: The pancreas suddenly starts producing extra insulin on its own

explanation: Brilliant! Healthy kidneys normally help clear out used insulin. When they are damaged, insulin hangs around in the blood longer, meaning you need less injected insulin. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h5)

question: What two hormones are found in Combined Oral Contraceptives?

options.A: Oxytocin and prolactin
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Testosterone and cortisol
options.D: Estrogen and progestin

explanation: COCs combine a synthetic estrogen and a synthetic progestin to reliably suppress the menstrual ovulation cycle. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h3)

question: How does community stigma usually affect a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: It immediately cures all physical infections without needing medicine
options.B: It forces humanitarian agencies to close down local counseling centers
options.C: It drives the survivor into isolation and prevents them from seeking help
options.D: It guarantees that the perpetrator will be publicly arrested by police

explanation: Fear of being judged or blamed makes survivors hide their pain and stay away from the clinics and help they desperately need. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h4)

question: How do cultural traditions in Nigeria often influence end-of-life care preferences?

options.A: Family members are legally barred from participating in bedside care
options.B: Families often prefer patients to spend their final days at home surrounded by relatives
options.C: Traditional practices completely replace all modern nursing interventions
options.D: Patients almost always request solitary care in private hospital rooms

explanation: In many Nigerian communities, passing on surrounded by family at home is a deeply cherished tradition, bringing great comfort to everyone involved. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of using a qualitative approach in a nursing study?

options.A: To find the exact percentage of patients cured by a drug
options.B: To measure the physical strength recovery of post-op clients
options.C: To gain a deep understanding of lived human experiences
options.D: To prove a mathematical relationship between two variables

explanation: Qualitative research helps us walk in our patients' shoes and truly understand what they are going through emotionally. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do many health workers hesitate to take up jobs in poor rural areas?

options.A: Medical equipment cannot function without advanced urban laboratory setups
options.B: Government policies forbid deploying trained professionals outside state capitals
options.C: Workers are reluctant to live in areas lacking basic infrastructure and security
options.D: Rural residents refuse to seek care from qualified nurses and midwives

explanation: Everyone wants a safe home, electricity, good schools for their kids, and basic amenities. Without these, rural postings are a hard sell. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h5)

question: A patient is nearly ready for independent life and only needs short-term guidance on budgeting and job hunting. Which facility fits best?

options.A: Transitional living facility
options.B: Long-term nursing home
options.C: Maximum security asylum
options.D: Acute psychiatric ward

explanation: You nailed it! Transitional facilities are short-term setups designed to help patients brush up on practical skills like managing money and finding jobs before they head out on their own. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to pour household cleaning chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.A: Bottled drinks cannot hold the weight of heavy industrial-strength soap
options.B: It causes the chemical solution to evaporate and lose its cleaning power completely
options.C: The plastic material used in beverage bottles reacts poorly with standard water
options.D: It increases the risk of accidental ingestion by mistaking the chemical for a drink

explanation: That's right! Putting chemicals in drink bottles is a major cause of accidental poisoning because someone might easily mistake it for a refreshing drink. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which of these items is a classic biological hazard you'll encounter on the wards?

options.A: Empty food containers from the cafeteria
options.B: Cardboard boxes from office supplies
options.C: Blood-soaked dressings and swabs
options.D: Expired non-prescription tablets

explanation: Correct! Items dripping or soaked with blood or body fluids carry active germs that can easily cause infections if not handled carefully. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common driver of trauma in many Nigerian communities today?

options.A: Widespread technological automation
options.B: Farmer-herder conflicts
options.C: Insurgency and banditry
options.D: Displacement from homes

explanation: You got it! While things like insecurity, banditry, and displacement cause real trauma, office and factory automation aren't major drivers of community trauma here. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T1#GNS314_U6_T1_h4)

question: An adult patient with severe liver disease starts bruising easily and bleeding from the gums. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: An acquired failure of the liver to produce clotting factors
options.B: An inherited defect in primary platelet aggregation
options.C: A congenital absence of von Willebrand factor
options.D: An inherited genetic mutation in the factor VIII gene

explanation: The liver is like the body's clotting factor factory! When it's sick, it can't make enough factors, leading to an acquired bleeding problem. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h2)

question: When is a simple hand wash with ordinary soap and water best to use?

options.A: After handling visibly soiled items or using the restroom
options.B: Immediately before inserting a central venous catheter
options.C: Before assisting in major open-heart surgery
options.D: When hands are completely dry and free of visible dirt

explanation: When your hands are visibly dirty or messy, plain soap and water are your best friends for a physical clean-up. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h4)

question: Two nurses have totally different working styles, which causes minor daily friction between them. How is the best way to view this?

options.A: One of the nurses must be fired immediately for misconduct
options.B: It is a normal interpersonal clash of styles rather than a moral failure
options.C: The hospital building design is entirely to blame for their frustration
options.D: They will eventually agree on everything if left alone long enough

explanation: People naturally work differently—some are fast-paced, others meticulous. Recognizing this as a simple style difference helps teams manage tension without making it personal. [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h3)

question: How is desiccated thyroid extract different from synthetic levothyroxine?

options.A: Both thyroxine and triiodothyronine from animal sources
options.B: Non-hormonal plant extracts that stimulate the pituitary
options.C: Only pure synthetic triiodothyronine
options.D: Chemically altered molecules designed to bypass the liver

explanation: Desiccated thyroid comes from dried animal glands, meaning it naturally carries a mix of thyroid hormones rather than just one lab-created formula. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T2#GNS223_U7_T2_h2)

question: What is the name of the muscular food pipe that connects your throat to your stomach?

options.A: Larynx
options.B: Pharynx
options.C: Trachea
options.D: Esophagus

explanation: Spot on! The esophagus is our dedicated highway for swallowing food down from the throat to the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which type of immunity is present from birth and reacts the same way to all foreign invaders?

options.A: Adaptive immunity
options.B: Artificial active immunity
options.C: Innate immunity
options.D: Natural passive immunity

explanation: Innate immunity is our built-in, non-specific defense system that responds immediately to any foreign threat without prior exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is usually the very first sign that a newborn is developing tetanus?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.B: Inability to suck or feed properly
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: High fever and watery diarrhea

explanation: Correct! Stiff jaw muscles make it hard for the baby to latch or suck, which is often the first warning sign mothers and nurses notice. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h4)

question: How does an autoclave sterilize infectious waste?

options.A: By freezing the waste to extremely low temperatures
options.B: By soaking the waste in strong liquid bleach
options.C: By using high-pressure steam to kill pathogens
options.D: By crushing the waste into tiny metal cubes

explanation: Autoclaves use heat, moisture, and high pressure to destroy infectious microorganisms effectively before disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: What is the main job of the tough outer shell (exoskeleton) on an insect?

options.A: Generating body heat during cold weather
options.B: Pumping oxygen directly into the insect bloodstream
options.C: Protecting internal organs and preventing water loss
options.D: Producing venom to paralyze small prey

explanation: That crunchy outer coat acts like a suit of armor that keeps the insect safe and stops it from drying out in the sun. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why should a nurse keep sentences short and clear when speaking to a disaster survivor?

options.A: Survivors usually have poor hearing after a disaster
options.B: Trauma and shock impair concentration and memory
options.C: Long sentences cost too much valuable time
options.D: Hospital regulations require brief communication

explanation: High stress levels make it difficult for survivors to process complex information or long explanations. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which anti-TB drug requires regular checks on a patient's vision and color sight?

options.A: Pyrazinamide
options.B: Isoniazid
options.C: Rifampin
options.D: Ethambutol

explanation: Ethambutol can affect eye health (optic neuritis). Regular eye checks help catch any vision changes early before they become serious. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h8)

question: Why is understanding a patient's home environment vital for a successful care plan?

options.A: It allows the nurse to charge appropriate hospital fees
options.B: It replaces the need for any physical assessment
options.C: It ensures the recommended treatment is realistic for their daily life
options.D: It prevents family members from visiting the ward

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing what life looks like at home helps us design treatment plans the patient can actually afford and manage. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h7)

question: In which part of the fallopian tube does fertilization of the ovum normally take place?

options.A: The ampulla
options.B: The fimbriae
options.C: The interstitial segment
options.D: The isthmus

explanation: The wider ampulla section provides the ideal space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the released egg. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h1)

question: What term do qualitative researchers use instead of traditional statistical terms like validity and reliability?

options.A: Trustworthiness
options.B: Numeric accuracy
options.C: Precision testing
options.D: Generalizability

explanation: Well done! Because qualitative work deals with stories and feelings rather than numbers, we check its quality by looking at its 'trustworthiness'. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h6)

question: A nurse notices her wrists resting hard against the sharp edge of the desk while typing patient notes. What is the best immediate adjustment?

options.A: Wear a thick leather weightlifting belt to improve core stability while charting
options.B: Stand up completely for all future documentation tasks during the shift
options.C: Tilt the computer monitor upward by forty-five degrees to change her line of sight
options.D: Reposition the keyboard and adjust her chair so wrists stay straight and unsupported by sharp edges

explanation: Spot on! Keeping your wrists free from sharp desk edges prevents annoying nerve compression and soft tissue pain. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: A patient recovering from an unsafe abortion looks quiet and won't speak to her family. What should you do first?

options.A: Call hospital security to watch for self-harm
options.B: Leave her alone in the ward until she asks for help
options.C: Demand an explanation of why she tried an illegal procedure
options.D: Sit quietly with her, listen with compassion, and promise privacy

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space builds trust and helps her share her emotional burden. Your empathy is your greatest nursing tool! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: What are the two main synthetic hormones used in most hormonal birth control methods?

options.A: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.B: Estrogen and progestin
options.C: Cortisol and aldosterone
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Great start! Hormonal contraceptives work by mimicking natural female hormones using synthetic forms of estrogen and progestin to keep the cycle regulated and prevent pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T011#GNS226_U6_T011_h1)

question: What is the top nursing priority right after major cancer surgery?

options.A: Withdrawing all intravenous fluids immediately
options.B: Preventing complications and managing acute surgical pain
options.C: Discharging the patient within twenty-four hours
options.D: Starting intensive physical exercise right away

explanation: Right after surgery, keeping your patient comfortable and watching out for issues like infection or blood clots are your most important duties. You are well on your way to becoming an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is showing empathy such a powerful tool in community nursing?

options.A: It eliminates the need to document nursing assessments.
options.B: It encourages patients to share sensitive information they might otherwise hide.
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will never experience chronic illness.
options.D: It allows the nurse to take over complete legal control of the household.

explanation: When patients feel safe and unjudged, they'll open up about the real struggles they face with their health. Empathy wins every time! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h4)

question: What is compulsory before a patient takes part in a nursing research study?

options.A: A financial deposit
options.B: Informed consent
options.C: Hospital employment
options.D: A government passport

explanation: Patients must always be fully informed about the study and willingly agree to participate of their own free will. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h7)

question: A patient uses an electric oxygen concentrator and lives where power outages are common. What must be in their safety plan?

options.A: An agreement to rely solely on battery-operated kitchen fans
options.B: Advice to stop using oxygen completely whenever it rains outside
options.C: A plan to drive to the hospital emergency room every single night
options.D: A backup battery system and instructions on handling a power failure

explanation: Oxygen-dependent clients need a reliable backup plan and power source so their breathing support doesn't cut out during a blackout. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is the link between physical disability and poverty in developing regions like Nigeria?

options.A: They share a cycle where each makes the other worse
options.B: Poverty completely protects people from impairments
options.C: Disability guarantees instant wealth
options.D: They have no connection at all

explanation: Poverty can lead to accidents and lack of healthcare (causing disability), and living with a disability can make earning an income harder. It's a tough cycle! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h2)

question: What term describes the number of new cases of a disease appearing during a specific time period?

options.A: Endemicity
options.B: Morbidity
options.C: Incidence
options.D: Prevalence

explanation: Incidence measures the frequency of newly developing cases of a disease in a population over a defined period. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h5)

question: A ward manager wants to change wound care based on one small, poorly designed study. What should the staff nurse do first?

options.A: Critique the study to see if the methods support the new practice
options.B: Report the journal publisher to the nursing council
options.C: Immediately adopt the new method without reading the paper
options.D: Refuse to do any wound care for the patients

explanation: Before changing clinical routines, nurses should examine the strength and validity of the underlying research. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is an obsession in someone dealing with obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: A physical movement done to relieve muscle tension
options.B: An intrusive and unwanted thought that causes anxiety
options.C: A sudden memory loss regarding personal identity
options.D: A complete loss of contact with external reality

explanation: Spot on! Think of an obsession as an unwelcome thought or image that keeps popping into the mind against the person's will, bringing along a lot of stress. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h1)

question: What usually happens if a family planning client never returns for follow-up checks?

options.A: They will experience guaranteed protection from sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They will automatically switch to a permanent surgical method
options.C: They may stop using their method incorrectly or face unmanaged side effects
options.D: They are required by law to pay a large financial penalty

explanation: Without our guidance during follow-ups, clients often struggle with side effects or make mistakes using their contraception, which makes them give up on it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: Who was a key pioneer of the Moral Treatment movement in France?

options.A: Sigmund Freud
options.B: Dorothea Dix
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Philippe Pinel

explanation: Philippe Pinel famously ordered the chains removed from patients in Paris asylums and introduced humane treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important to treat chronic pain promptly in a physically disabled patient?

options.A: Pain always causes immediate permanent paralysis
options.B: Untreated pain speeds up the digestive system dangerously
options.C: Pain can limit their ability to participate in rehabilitation therapy
options.D: Pain medication is the only way to prevent skin ulcers

explanation: When pain is poorly controlled, patients cannot engage in vital physical therapy exercises needed to maintain mobility. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of community herd immunity?

options.A: To guarantee lifelong immunity against common viral colds
options.B: To protect vulnerable individuals who cannot safely receive vaccines
options.C: To ensure pharmaceutical companies produce enough medication
options.D: To completely eliminate the need for hand hygiene in hospitals

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, shielding babies or sick patients who cannot get immunized. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary goal in the medical management of acute gastroenteritis?

options.A: Replacing lost fluids and electrolytes
options.B: Stopping the bowel movements immediately
options.C: Placing the patient on a strict zero-food diet
options.D: Giving strong antibiotics to kill all viruses

explanation: Preventing or correcting dehydration is the single most important intervention to save lives in gastroenteritis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: A nurse sets up a desk in the village square to check blood sugar levels for healthy adults. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Quaternary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: You nailed it! Screening tests catch health issues early before big symptoms show up, which is what secondary prevention is all about. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h3)

question: A patient with a bad skin infection suddenly has a high fever, fast heart rate, and low blood pressure. What is happening?

options.A: Chronic contact dermatitis
options.B: Systemic sepsis
options.C: Superficial fungal infection
options.D: Localized scar formation

explanation: Spot on! These are classic warning signs that an infection has spread into the bloodstream, leading to dangerous sepsis. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T11#GNS213_U5_T11_h3)

question: Which medication is routinely given during antenatal visits to protect pregnant women and babies from malaria?

options.A: Chloroquine phosphate
options.B: Amodiaquine tablets
options.C: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
options.D: Quinine hydrochloride

explanation: Well done! Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) is given at set clinic visits to clear malaria parasites from the placenta and keep the baby safe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h5)

question: What should a nurse focus on when assessing a pregnant patient for constipation?

options.A: The blood pressure reading taken in the right arm
options.B: Exclusively the heartbeat of the developing fetus
options.C: Stool consistency, straining effort, and dietary habits
options.D: Only the exact weight of the patient on the scale

explanation: Spot on! To truly help, we need to ask about how hard the stool is, if she struggles to push, and what she's been eating and drinking. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h4)

question: In a life-threatening poisoning emergency, which route of administration is generally preferred for antidotes?

options.A: Intravenous
options.B: Transdermal
options.C: Subcutaneous
options.D: Rectal suppository

explanation: The IV route puts the antidote straight into the bloodstream so it can start working almost immediately when every second counts. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h5)

question: How do vocational and peer support programs help a patient newly released on parole?

options.A: They completely replace the need for antipsychotic medications.
options.B: They rebuild daily routines, confidence, and social connections.
options.C: They guarantee that the patient will never feel stressed again.
options.D: They allow the legal system to close the patient's case file forever.

explanation: You got it! Healing goes beyond just stopping symptoms; patients need help rebuilding their confidence, daily habits, and friendships. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why does the anterior pituitary gland enlarge during normal pregnancy?

options.A: Enlargement due to retained fluid volume
options.B: Proliferation of prolactin-secreting cells
options.C: Hypertrophy of cells producing growth hormone
options.D: Increased storage of oxytocin for delivery

explanation: The anterior pituitary grows noticeably larger because the cells that produce prolactin multiply rapidly to prepare the mother's body for breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h2)

question: A hospitalized patient snaps angrily at a nurse, complaining that the room is too loud and care is terrible. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Report the patient to the attending physician for verbal abuse
options.B: Argue back to set firm boundaries on respectful communication
options.C: Understand the frustration is a normal part of grief and remain calm
options.D: Leave the room immediately and refuse to return that shift

explanation: Taking anger personally interferes with care; recognizing it as a stage of grief helps maintain a therapeutic relationship. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which lab pattern is typical for untreated hypoparathyroidism?

options.A: Low serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.B: Low serum calcium and high serum phosphate
options.C: High serum calcium and normal parathyroid hormone
options.D: High serum calcium and low serum phosphate

explanation: Without enough PTH to boost calcium, your blood calcium drops (hypocalcemia) and your PTH levels remain low. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h4)

question: A patient with a head injury shows unstable vital signs and irregular breathing. Which part of the brain is most likely affected?

options.A: Brainstem

question: Why shouldn't you pour leftover liquid medicines down a regular sink drain?

options.D: It produces toxic gases inside the nursing station

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge facing rural Primary Health Care?

question: Why do different health workers come together as a team in community health?

question: What is the main goal of supported housing for patients on psychiatric parole?

question: How is persistent depressive disorder different from major depressive disorder?

question: How do good communication skills help families stay healthy?

question: Which common issue involves the compression of the median nerve in the wrist?

question: How does cultural stigma affect the two-way referral process?

question: Why is classifying emergencies especially vital when many patients arrive at once?

options.C: It ensures all patients are treated in the exact order of arrival

question: Which of these is NOT a typical system-level cause of unsafe injections in resource-limited settings?

question: A nursing mother says she cannot afford expensive baby formula or imported supplements. As a nurse, what is your best response?

question: What is the main goal of Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)?

options.A: To suppress viral replication and reduce the viral load to undetectable levels

options.C: To completely eliminate the HIV virus from every cell in the body
options.D: To cure advanced stages of AIDS within two weeks of treatment

explanation: While ART doesn't clear every single trace of the virus, it puts a heavy brake on it, lowering the viral load so the immune system can bounce back and stay strong. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when setting new objectives for a healthcare unit?

question: What is the main reason for running routine daily or weekly self-tests on an AED?

options.B: Ensure the device is functional and ready for an emergency
options.C: Calibrate the internal software to match local voltage standards

question: Which condition means a patient must NEVER be given misoprostol?

question: In mass casualty triage, what does a RED tag mean?

options.B: Immediate, life-threatening injuries requiring urgent intervention to save life
options.C: Stable injuries that can safely wait several hours for medical attention

question: What is the main goal of performing the Romberg test during a physical exam?

question: What tells your kidneys to release erythropoietin (EPO) to make more red blood cells?

question: Why do we love using the metric system in healthcare?

question: How do long-term high food prices contribute to chronic illnesses like diabetes and obesity in vulnerable communities?

question: Which part of the cell is usually targeted by poisons that block energy and ATP production?

question: What statistical measurement is primarily used in case-control studies?

question: Which statement best describes the role of most microorganisms found in food?

question: What is the main job of prostaglandins when childbirth is about to start?

question: What is the best way for a nurse to care for an FGM survivor in the clinic?

question: What body regulates the Nurse Practice Act and professional standards for nurses in Nigeria?

question: Why is spotting delivery complications early at a primary health centre so crucial?

question: Which activity is a great example of 'organizing' on a clinical ward?

question: Who is most important to involve when trying to change harmful food taboos in a rural community?

question: You want to prove your ICU needs more staff than a general ward. Which tool is best to use?

question: What is the primary focus of neurological nursing?

question: What is a major challenge facing families who seek formal custodial care in urban Nigerian cities?

options.A: High out-of-pocket costs because insurance rarely covers non-medical care
options.B: Strict government laws that forbid hiring private home caregivers

explanation: Because health insurance typically covers acute medical care rather than long-term custodial help, families must pay out of pocket for private aides. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: What does the term 'oophoritis' mean?

options.A: Swelling of the fallopian tubes
options.B: Cyst formation on the cervix

options.D: Infection of the uterine lining

question: What triggers a homeostatic imbalance in the human body?

options.A: When a person sleeps for more than eight hours

options.C: When vital signs stay completely stable for a long time
options.D: When the body eats a balanced diet with fresh fruits

question: What is the best and most reliable way to confirm a multiple pregnancy?

options.A: Maternal blood pressure

options.C: Fundal height palpation
options.D: Stethoscope auscultation

explanation: Spot on! An ultrasound gives us a clear picture, letting us count the gestational sacs and heartbeats early on. Modern tech makes midwifery so exciting! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h3)

question: How do correlational studies usually help prepare for future clinical trials?

options.A: By replacing the need for any human participants in the lab
options.B: By proving beyond doubt that a treatment cures a disease
options.C: By showing that a relationship exists to justify further research
options.D: By randomly assigning patients to control and treatment groups

explanation: Brilliant! Finding a solid connection in a correlational study gives scientists the green light to invest time and money into bigger experiments. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should figure out before teaching a patient at home?

options.A: How the patient and family process information
options.B: The exact brand of television in the living room
options.C: The cost of the patient's home insurance policy
options.D: How many bedrooms the house contains

explanation: Always check their literacy level, language preferences, and how they learn best so your teaching actually makes sense to them. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and release hormones directly into the blood
options.B: Exocrine glands possess a rich network of fenestrated capillaries
options.C: Endocrine glands secrete substances exclusively onto the skin surface
options.D: Exocrine glands produce chemical messengers while endocrine glands do not

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems! Because they don't have tubes (ducts), they dump their hormones straight into the bloodstream to travel round the body. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which leadership style uses a system of rewards and punishments to manage staff?

options.A: Authentic leadership
options.B: Situational leadership
options.C: Transformational leadership
options.D: Transactional leadership

explanation: Think 'transaction'—you do this task well, you get rewarded; you make a mistake, you face correction. That's transactional leadership! [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why are typhoid and paratyphoid fevers grouped together as 'enteric fevers'?

options.A: They share very similar clinical presentations and transmission routes
options.B: They can both be cured within twenty-four hours of symptom onset
options.C: They only affect individuals living in cold climates
options.D: They are both caused by viral pathogens affecting the respiratory system

explanation: Spot on! Because they look alike in patients and spread the same way through the gut, we group them together as enteric fevers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h1)

question: Why is 'Disturbed Body Image' a common nursing diagnosis for conditions like Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Visible physical changes like weight gain and facial swelling alter a person's appearance.
options.B: Hormonal imbalances cause permanent memory loss and confusion.
options.C: Severe muscle weakness prevents the patient from looking in a mirror.
options.D: Patients lose their sense of hearing and balance due to inner ear fluid shifts.

explanation: Spot on. Cushing's brings noticeable body changes, like round 'moon facies' and weight shifts, which can be really tough on a patient's self-esteem. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which phase of the menstrual cycle comes immediately after ovulation?

options.A: The luteal phase
options.B: The menstrual phase
options.C: The proliferative phase
options.D: The follicular phase

explanation: Right after ovulation, the cycle enters the luteal phase. This is when the leftover follicle forms the corpus luteum to produce progesterone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why do healthcare workers give naloxone to a patient who has overdosed on heroin or morphine?

options.A: To cure the underlying addiction permanently
options.B: To lower their elevated blood pressure
options.C: To stop dangerous breathing depression by blocking opioid receptors
options.D: To speed up the breakdown of the drug in the liver

explanation: Exactly! Opioids dangerously slow down breathing. Naloxone quickly kicks them off the receptors and revives the patient's breathing drive. A true lifesaver! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which popular fruit juice is well known for interfering with gut enzymes and dangerously raising blood levels of certain drugs?

options.A: Grapefruit juice
options.B: Filtered tap water
options.C: Fresh cow milk
options.D: Green tea infusion

explanation: Grapefruit juice is a classic pharmacological troublemaker! It blocks specific enzymes in your gut, letting way too much of a drug slip into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a major benefit of using physiological measures like a blood pressure machine in research?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any human researchers
options.B: They cost nothing to purchase and maintain
options.C: They take the place of nursing clinical judgment
options.D: They provide objective data that cannot be falsified by memory

explanation: Physiological tools measure physical states directly, providing reliable, objective data without relying on patient memory. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h5)

question: What role does the environment play in keeping an endemic disease going?

options.A: It builds permanent immunity inside the bloodstream of the host
options.B: It provides external conditions that bring the agent and host together
options.C: It acts as the biological organism that manufactures the toxins
options.D: It develops pharmaceutical treatments to cure the infected population

explanation: Things like warm weather or stagnant water create the right setting for germs and vectors to find human hosts easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h3)

question: What is the main transmission route for most water-borne pathogens?

options.A: The fecal-oral route
options.B: Skin contact with soil
options.C: Direct airborne droplets
options.D: Mosquito bite vectors

explanation: Water-borne diseases spread when microscopic fecal matter contaminates drinking or food preparation water, which is then swallowed. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h4)

question: How is healthcare 'need' different from healthcare 'demand'?

options.A: There is no practical difference between need and demand in a well-functioning hospital
options.B: Demand is determined entirely by doctors, while need is controlled by health insurance companies
options.C: Need is a clinical judgment of required care, while demand is based on consumer willingness and ability to pay
options.D: Need only applies to surgical procedures, while demand applies exclusively to prescription drugs

explanation: Exactly! As a nurse, you see what the patient clinically needs. But market demand only happens when they can actually afford and agree to pay for that care. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h2)

question: A nurse notices women suffering from regular coughs and eye irritation because they cook daily with firewood in closed kitchens. What is the main culprit here?

options.A: A contagious bacterial lung infection spreading through handshakes
options.B: Indoor air pollution from inadequate ventilation and smoke
options.C: Severe vitamin deficiency caused by poor farming output
options.D: Direct allergic reaction to new insecticides used outdoors

explanation: Cooking with firewood in rooms without good windows traps heavy smoke inside, irritating the eyes and lungs over time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T9#GNS122_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why do inhaled anesthetic gases exit the body so quickly through the lungs?

options.A: They easily cross the tiny air sacs (alveoli) from the blood right into the lungs.
options.B: Inhaled gases bind tightly to red blood cells until reaching the lungs.
options.C: The kidneys cannot filter gases, so the lungs are the only option.
options.D: Lung tissue actively pumps anesthetic molecules out into the room air.

explanation: Once a patient stops breathing the anesthesia gas, the gas dissolved in their blood naturally crosses the thin air sac membranes when they exhale, clearing it out fast. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the proper nursing action when a competent patient insists on leaving the hospital before treatment is complete?

options.A: Explain the risks and have them sign a discharge against medical advice form
options.B: Ignore the request and refuse to give them their personal clothes
options.C: Call the police immediately to physically lock the patient inside the room
options.D: Hide the patient's shoes so they cannot walk out of the ward

explanation: A competent adult has the right to leave, but the nurse must warn them of potential dangers and document the event by having them sign a DAMA form. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h7)

question: What kind of authority does a nurse have when others listen to them purely because of their special clinical skills and advanced training?

options.A: Traditional authority
options.B: Charismatic authority
options.C: Formal authority
options.D: Expert authority

explanation: Brilliant! When respect and obedience come from your deep knowledge and specialized skills, that's your 'expert authority' shining through. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h2)

question: As a nurse in an IDP camp, you notice a sudden spike in watery diarrhea among children. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Contaminated drinking water sources
options.B: A sudden increase in local mosquito populations
options.C: Genetically inherited chronic bowel disorders
options.D: Routine administration of oral polio vaccines

explanation: Waterborne outbreaks like cholera or diarrhea are usually linked to unsafe drinking water in temporary settlements. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T20#GNS225_U5_T20_h2)

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a nurse on a hospital ward?

options.A: Being immune from any form of peer review or performance evaluation
options.B: Working night shifts without physical security guards on the ward
options.C: Never experiencing stress or fatigue during clinical duties
options.D: Feeling safe to report errors and speak up without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: You got it! Psychological safety means trust—knowing you can speak up honestly to protect your patients. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the main use of a family planning client register in the clinic?

options.A: To record detailed client information and services given sequentially
options.B: To track daily weather patterns affecting clinic attendance
options.C: To advertise new contraceptive brands to visiting community members
options.D: To list the financial debts owed by the local health facility

question: What is the most important infection control habit for a nurse to teach a patient on immunosuppressive drugs?

options.A: Stopping all physical exercise completely
options.B: Wearing heavy winter clothing outside at all times
options.C: Drinking only distilled water
options.D: Doing thorough and frequent hand hygiene

explanation: Never underestimate the power of clean hands! Proper hand hygiene is your patient's number one defense against picking up harmful germs in everyday life. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the best way to help an older, weak patient who has a very poor appetite?

options.A: Providing nutrient-dense small meals and a pleasant dining setting
options.B: Withdrawing all food until the patient requests a heavy meal
options.C: Restricting fluid intake to prevent bathroom trips
options.D: Forcing large meals three times a day regardless of complaints

explanation: Well done! Small, rich portions are much easier for a weak patient to finish without feeling overwhelmed. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h6)

question: What makes 'probability sampling' special compared to other methods?

options.A: The researcher hand-picks participants who have the most interesting medical history

options.C: Participants are recruited strictly on a first-come, first-served hospital entry basis

question: Which screening tool is commonly used to check for delirium in ventilated ICU patients?

question: You are an unscrubbed nurse walking past a sterile table. What is the safest way to move around it?

options.C: Walk close behind the scrub nurse's back

question: Why is blood pressure in the pulmonary circulation much lower than in systemic circulation?

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to effective delegation by a nurse manager?

question: What role does the school nurse commonly play in supporting student mental health?

options.A: Grading students on mental health examinations

question: What happens during the peer-review process before a study is published?

question: Why is it risky to blindly trust BCMA without double-checking things yourself?

question: Why do we grab a cold pack immediately after someone suffers a fresh joint sprain?

options.C: To dilate vessels and increase local bleeding

question: Why do nurses pre-test IEC support materials before mass production?

options.C: To increase the market price of the printed paper leaflets

explanation: Pre-testing saves time and money by making sure people actually understand the pictures and text before you print thousands of copies. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h6)

question: A patient with high cholesterol uses butter for all their cooking. What heart-healthy swap can you suggest?

options.D: Solid shortening

question: Which of these is NOT a factor contributing to high maternal mortality in Nigeria?

question: Why do we generally recommend complex carbohydrates over simple sugars for psychiatric patients?

question: A public health team monitors school absenteeism and pharmacy sales of cough syrup during a flu season. What type of surveillance is this?

question: Which piece of equipment is usually missing on a standard ship?

options.C: Advanced imaging like CT scanners and MRIs
options.D: Basic digital blood pressure cuffs

question: What are the normal blood vessels found inside a healthy newborn umbilical cord?

options.D: One artery and one vein

question: Which of these actions is a serious example of research misconduct?

options.D: Making up survey results to match what you want to prove

question: A nurse is counseling a couple on birth preparedness. Which action is most important for them to plan before the due date?

options.C: Buying expensive nursery furniture for the baby
options.D: Arranging reliable transportation to the health facility

question: A patient comes in with sudden, severe watery diarrhea after drinking untreated water near a broken sewage pipe. Which condition is most likely?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Rheumatic fever

question: When giving eye drops, where is the safest spot to place the liquid?

question: Which of the following is classified as Type IV FGM?

question: Why should you wipe away the very first drop of blood after a finger prick?

question: What is the main goal of psychological first aid (PFA) when used by nurses in an IDP camp?

options.C: To diagnose underlying personality disorders in adults

question: A patient asks why they got a non-opioid cough syrup instead of a codeine-based one. What is the major benefit here?

options.C: Total absence of any side effects

question: An older adult with known dementia suddenly becomes very confused and agitated over twenty-four hours. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Normal psychological adjustment to changing weather patterns in the ward

options.C: Complete recovery from their cognitive deficits due to sudden rest
options.D: A permanent and irreversible acceleration of their underlying Alzheimer's disease

question: What is a simple way nurses can help reduce the emotional burden of isolation?

options.C: Spend time talking with the patient and use video calls to connect with family

question: Why does the autonomic nervous system use a two-neuron chain instead of just one?

question: Why do doctors often use numbing spray and a nasal decongestant before a flexible scope goes into the nose?

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to handle used needles?

question: What determines whether a person is considered Rh-positive?

options.C: The presence of both A and B antigens on their platelets
options.D: The total volume of hemoglobin circulating in their blood

question: When a patient is resting peacefully after a good meal, which part of their nervous system is hard at work?

options.B: Central integrative division
options.C: Parasympathetic division
options.D: Somatic motor division

question: Which of the following does NOT happen during untreated status epilepticus?

question: At what point in the hospital workflow should waste segregation take place?

options.A: Inside the municipal waste truck during transit to the dump site
options.B: At the final incineration plant before burning begins
options.C: At the exact point of origin where the waste is generated
options.D: By the sanitary inspectors during their weekly hospital visits

explanation: Spot on! Sorting must happen immediately at the bedside or treatment area so hazardous and general waste never mix. Brilliant! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the big danger if you fail to mix a diluted lotion thoroughly?

options.A: Extending the expiration date by several months
options.B: Turning the entire mixture into a watery liquid
options.C: Creating concentrated hot spots that irritate the skin
options.D: Changing the color of the cream to bright yellow

explanation: If you don't mix it well, pockets of high-strength medicine can hide in the cream and sting the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h8)

question: What is the main goal of doing a 'medication reconciliation' when a patient is admitted?

options.A: To compare home medications with new orders and prevent errors
options.B: To ensure the patient has enough food to take with their pills
options.C: To calculate the financial cost of the patient's prescriptions
options.D: To test how fast the patient's liver metabolizes oral tablets

explanation: Medication reconciliation is like doing a safety checkup on what the patient was taking at home versus what the doctor just prescribed, ensuring no dangerous overlaps slip through! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h6)

question: What does a vulnerability assessment help a healthcare team figure out?

options.A: The personal home addresses of all senior hospital administrative staff
options.B: The exact daily profit margins of local pharmaceutical retail stores
options.C: Which nursing students achieved the highest grades in community health
options.D: Which populations and structures are most at risk during a local hazard

explanation: Spot-on! A vulnerability assessment helps us see who in the community is most likely to suffer, letting us protect them first. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h5)

question: If your goal is to learn proper aseptic technique for surgery, which activity best helps you achieve it?

options.A: Listening to an audio podcast about common surgical instruments
options.B: Practicing sterile gloving and gowning in a skills laboratory
options.C: Writing a three-page essay on the history of hospital hygiene
options.D: Watching a movie depicting a busy hospital emergency room

explanation: To learn a physical skill, you've got to practice it hands-on in the lab! Theory is important, but action makes it stick. [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h4)

question: Which strategy is most important when trying to shift a hospital's workplace culture?

options.A: Sending out a single memo explaining the new hospital mission statement
options.B: Threatening disciplinary action for anyone who questions hospital leadership
options.C: Implementing deliberate, sustained actions that embed new values into daily work
options.D: Replacing all senior nursing staff with new graduates from local universities

explanation: Spot on! Changing culture doesn't happen from a single memo; it takes consistent, long-term effort built into everyday ward routines. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h5)

question: How should you handle a patient who strongly resists making healthy lifestyle changes?

options.A: Demand immediate compliance because the nurse knows best
options.B: Discontinue all nursing visits until the patient changes their attitude
options.C: Acknowledge the patient's feelings and explore the root cause of hesitation
options.D: Threaten to report the patient to local health authorities

explanation: Commands and threats never work well in nursing. Partner with your patient, listen to their worries, and solve problems together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h6)

question: What do the letters in the CAGE questionnaire stand for?

options.A: Control, Addicted, Grief, Escape
options.B: Crave, Anxiety, Guilt, Energy loss
options.C: Count, Assess, Guide, Evaluate
options.D: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener

explanation: The CAGE acronym helps clinicians remember four quick screening questions about cutting down, annoyance, guilt, and morning drinking. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h5)

question: What happens if clinic staff ignore their daily logs and stock registers?

options.A: Patients will automatically receive better care from nursing staff
options.B: The government will instantly increase the facility's monthly budget
options.C: Infection control practices become strictly enforced by default
options.D: Stockouts of essential medicines may go unnoticed until supplies completely run out

explanation: Keeping daily records helps you spot when drugs are running low so you can reorder before empty shelves catch you by surprise. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good public health practice for controlling disease-carrying flies and mosquitoes?

options.A: Leaving stagnant pools of water uncovered around homes
options.B: Clearing bushes and proper disposal of household refuse
options.C: Ensuring proper drainage systems in urban neighborhoods
options.D: Treating pit latrines with approved larvicides

explanation: Leaving water pools uncovered is an open invitation for mosquitoes and flies to breed! Good environmental health keeps communities safe. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h7)

question: How do waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid usually spread?

options.A: Inhalation of mist from clean cooling towers
options.B: Direct skin contact with industrial chemical waste
options.C: Mosquito bites near stagnant ponds and rivers
options.D: Ingestion of water contaminated with fecal matter

explanation: Correct! These nasty bugs spread mainly when people swallow food or water that has come into contact with human or animal waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h4)

question: Why does a low count of CD4+ T cells make a person vulnerable to many different infections?

options.A: CD4+ cells act as master coordinators that signal other immune cells to fight germs.
options.B: CD4+ cells are responsible for carrying oxygen to fighting white cells.
options.C: CD4+ cells physically trap and digest bacteria in the bloodstream.
options.D: CD4+ cells produce thick mucus barriers on skin and mucous membranes.

explanation: Think of CD4+ cells as the generals in an army. Without them giving orders, the rest of the immune defenses don't know when or how to attack germs! [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h2)

question: A male patient with severe chest pain waited three days to visit the clinic because he felt he had to 'be strong' for his family. Which concept best explains this delay?

options.A: An innate genetic flaw in male chromosome pairing
options.B: Socially constructed gender roles influencing health-seeking behavior
options.C: A standard physiological reaction to low blood pressure
options.D: An intersex hormonal imbalance affecting pain receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Traditional masculine expectations to be stoic can sadly stop men from seeking quick medical attention. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h6)
